author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis reached Perim Island in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on Friday, according to four Yemeni government sources cited by Reuters. Two sources said Saudi-backed government forces had withdrawn from the island after the Houthis also took the mainland town of Dhubab, which faces it.

Perim sits at the mouth of a shipping lane connecting the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden. Control of the island could increase pressure on commercial traffic at a time when the Strait of Hormuz is already severely disrupted, forcing more attention onto the western route used by Saudi energy shipments.

The movement is a material extension of the Houthis’ rapid coastal advance. Yemeni government forces said they plan to deploy weapons and aircraft in an effort to retake captured areas and warned civilians to avoid a route between Taiz and Mocha. The Houthis captured Mocha and the Hanish islands on Thursday.

The situation remains fluid, and control on the ground may change as government forces organize a counteroffensive. The immediate risk extends beyond Yemen: any sustained disruption at Bab el-Mandeb could affect shipping schedules, insurance costs and energy supply routes linking Asia, the Middle East and Europe.
dek: Yemeni government forces withdrew from the strategic island as the group’s rapid Red Sea advance raised pressure on a vital shipping corridor.
headline: Houthis reach Perim Island at mouth of Bab el-Mandeb
